entities.summary:
André Du Ryer, Lord of La Garde-Malezair, was a French orientalist who produced L'Alcoran de Mahomet, the third western translation of the Quran. This achievement mattered in the early 17th-century intellectual landscape of Western Europe, where the study of Islam and Arabic language was gaining momentum. The translation of the Quran into European languages facilitated a deeper understanding of Islamic theology and culture, paving the way for future orientalists and scholars of the Islamic world.

Born in 1580 in Marcigny, France, Du Ryer was a key figure in the development of French orientalism during the Renaissance. His work was heavily influenced by the likes of Guillaume Budé and Jacques César de Commines, who had previously translated Arabic texts into Latin.

Du Ryer's translation of L'Alcoran de Mahomet, completed in 1668, was a significant milestone in the history of Islamic studies in Europe. The work showcased Du Ryer's mastery of Arabic language and literature, as well as his ability to contextualize Islamic concepts within the framework of Christian theology.

Du Ryer's legacy extends beyond his own work, as it influenced subsequent generations of scholars and orientalists. His translation of the Quran into European languages helped to bridge the gap between East and West, facilitating a greater understanding of Islamic culture and theology.

Du Ryer's remarkable translation, which took over 100 years to complete, is a testament to his unwavering dedication to the study of Arabic language and literature. The work remains an important milestone in the history of Islamic studies in Europe, and its impact can still be felt today.
